properties.decision: RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-07-25, from work he has done: State Funerals for US Presidents (he worked President Bush's) — hundreds to thousands of people planning simultaneously, an echeloned plan (NORTHCOM OPLAN → JTF-NCR → each service → each unit), and events arriving during the run that the plan must react to in minutes. His words: "using a common github repo may no longer work". THE DECOMPOSITION THAT MAKES IT TRACTABLE IS ALREADY DECIDED: dec:nested-graphs (c) says a design is its own graph per ownership boundary, so a thousand planners are not a thousand writers on one store — they are ~100-200 graphs of 5-20 writers each, linked by mirrored published surfaces. Echelons own their plans; that is both the software answer and how the organisation actually works. FOUR ROADS for the tier itself. (a) NOTHING NEW — federation plus git, accepting minutes of latency; cheapest, and it fails only the react-in-near-real-time half. (b) ONE PROCESS PER GRAPH over streamable HTTP (rmcp has the transport, reflow2 serves stdio only), writes going to the store and the export DERIVED as the archival record; at federation scale the process-per-project cut already named in dec:central-host is also the natural sharding — one process per ownership boundary is one staff. (c) ONE SHARED MULTI-WRITER STORE, which means replacing single-writer RocksDB and owning consensus; most work, least alignment with a design that already shards by authority. (d) EVENT-SOURCED LOG plus materialised views — attractive because a plan IS a change history, expensive because every detector currently reads a materialised graph. WHAT BREAKS TODAY, in order: single-writer per graph (the six-seat outage of 2026-07-25 was this at tiny scale), the whole-document write path (769 KB for 606 nodes; a funeral federation is 10^5-10^6 nodes changing continuously), git-round-trip latency, nothing that pushes, no identity or authorization, and req:stale-seat-knows going from one bad afternoon to a systemic property.
properties.name: OPEN — does reflow2 grow a live tier for hundreds of simultaneous planners, alongside the repo file?
properties.rationale: Held as brainstorming because it is explicitly distant-future ("probably distant future") and because it challenges the PREMISE of two decisions rather than their reasoning — which is the honest thing to record, not to act on. dec:multi-writer-architecture chose repo-file-plus-merge on a rationale resting on concurrency being hypothetical; dec:central-host's rationale says outright that this tool "does not need" simultaneity "and may be harmed by it". A thousand people replanning a state funeral under events is the named counter-case both were missing, and per dec:reopen-supersedes the move is a new decision point, never flipping those back. NOTE THE PART THAT NEEDS NO DECISION: the ownership boundary federation already draws is the natural AUTHORIZATION boundary — you write your echelon's graph and read your superior's published surface — so authz needs enforcement, not a new concept, and Interface.designation internal|published is already the read primitive. Also settled by inspection: ordering without a shared git history needs no global clock, because the same federation shape gives a total order WITHIN each boundary (the store, proved by the content-hash chain) and dated coordinates ACROSS boundaries (a mirror already carries whose design, which version, when) — exactly how echelons coordinate. Full reasoning in docs/planning-at-scale.md.
